No web search, no standout source or repository, no other repositories.

Two things beyond docs/ that I should name precisely:

(a) Compiler-driven probing of the public API, for one thing docs/ does not
spell out. `docs/topics/app-configuration.md` shows `.context_fn("timestamp",
|_ctx| { Value::from(...) })` without naming the parameter type, its import
path, or which `Value`. I wrote deliberately wrong code and read rustc's
diagnostics: `expected closure signature 'for<'a, 'b> fn(&'a RenderContext<'b>)
-> _'`, then `expected '()', found '&Value'` for `ctx.data`, then `expected
'minijinja::value::Value', found 'serde_json::value::Value'` for the return.
That is how I learned the provider is `|ctx: &standout::context::RenderContext|
-> minijinja::Value` with `ctx.data: &serde_json::Value`. One of those
diagnostics printed a path into the vendored crate source
(`standout-9.0.0/src/cli/builder/config.rs:28`); I did not open that file or
any other standout source file.

(b) Empirical probing of the compiled framework. Before writing the real app I
built a throwaway command in `app/` and ran it to answer questions docs/ leaves
open — what a template sees when handler data is a bare `Vec<T>`, what reaches
stdout when a template renders to the empty string, the exact stderr bytes and
status of `ExternalFailure`, which stream a naked invocation writes to. All of
that came from running the binary, not from reading standout's code.

(c) General (non-standout) prior knowledge: Rust, clap 4 derive, serde and
`#[serde(untagged)]`, and Jinja/MiniJinja syntax — filters (`map(attribute=…)`,
`map("length")`, `max`, `join`), whitespace-control markers (`{%-`/`-%}`), and
recursive macros. docs/ points at MiniJinja for exactly this and doesn't
restate the syntax, so I used what I already knew and then checked each
construct against the running binary.

answers.docs.gaps:
(1) Missing: what a template sees when handler data is not a map.
`docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md` says only "**Output must be
Serialize**: Needed for JSON/YAML modes and template context", and both it and
`intro-to-dispatch.md` show `HandlerResult<Vec<Item>>` as a normal return type.
What actually happens is that a `Vec` root leaves the template with no bindings
at all — every lookup is undefined and renders as the empty string. Since the
handler's return type is simultaneously the JSON root and the template context,
this is a real design constraint for any command whose machine contract is an
array, and no page states it. The `context_fn` escape hatch exists and works,
but nothing connects the two topics.

(2) Wrong: `docs/guides/intro-to-testing.md` — "The `serial_test::serial`
attribute is re-exported from `standout_test` for convenience: `use
standout_test::serial;`". Following that alone gives `error[E0433]: cannot find
module or crate `serial_test` in this scope`, because the macro expands to code
that names `serial_test`. The `[dev-dependencies]` snippet on that same page
lists only `standout-test = "9"`.

(3) Missing: `docs/topics/app-configuration.md`'s `context_fn` example
(`.context_fn("terminal_width", |ctx| { Value::from(ctx.terminal_width...) })`)
names neither the parameter type nor an import for it nor which `Value` is
meant, and "Dynamic providers receive `RenderContext` with output mode,
terminal width, and handler data" does not say the handler data is reached as
`ctx.data` or that it is a `serde_json::Value` while the return must be a
`minijinja::Value`. `docs/crates/render/topics/template-engines.md` shows
`standout_render::context::RenderContext`, which is not the path that resolves
from a lone `standout` dependency (`standout::context::RenderContext` is).

(4) Small: `docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md` documents the
trailing-newline contract precisely, which was genuinely useful, but says
nothing about the empty render. Empirically a template that renders to `""`
produces zero bytes on stdout — not the one `\n` that "`App::run` writes a
handled command's text with `writeln!`" would suggest. That is the behaviour
`brewlike deps <leaf>` needs, and I would rather it were stated than probed.
answers.friction:
(1) The biggest one: a handler whose data has an array or scalar root is
invisible to its own template. The spec requires that `brewlike list --output
json` be "an array of formula records", and `docs/crates/render/topics/
templating.md` says structured modes are `serde_json::to_string_pretty(data)`,
so the handler must return a bare `Vec<FormulaRecord>`. docs/ shows exactly
that shape — `docs/crates/dispatch/guides/intro-to-dispatch.md`: "fn
list_handler(_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Vec<Item>>"
— but nothing says what the template then binds. Probing with a template of
`items:[{{ items }}] data:[{{ data }}] value:[{{ value }}]` against a handler
returning `Vec<Item>` printed `items:[] data:[] value:[]`: every name is
undefined, because the MiniJinja context is the data itself and a sequence has
no keys. So the array root and the human rendering are in direct tension, and
the only documented way out is `AppBuilder::context_fn`, which
`docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md` describes as template-only ("When
handler data and context variables have the same key, handler data wins.
Context is supplementary") and `docs/topics/app-configuration.md` says
receives "handler data". That is what I used.

(2) `context_fn`'s own signature is undocumented (see 3a): three compile-error
round trips to get from the doc's `|ctx| { Value::from(ctx.terminal_width...) }`
to a provider that compiles.

(3) The spec's table rule — "each column but the last padded with trailing
spaces to the width of its widest rendered cell, header included" — is exactly
what `tabular()` does not do. `docs/crates/render/guides/intro-to-tabular.md`:
"A `{"min": ..., "max": ...}` column is resolved once, when `tabular()` or
`table()` builds the formatter, before any row is seen — it does not measure
row content. […] Resolving a top-level column's width from every row's content
— the whole table, not just one row — is issue #359". So I computed the width
in the template instead and fed it to `col`:
`{%- set name_width = (["FORMULA"] + (view | map(attribute="name") | list)) |
map("length") | max -%}`.

(4) An application cannot own its own error prose on the ordinary path.
`docs/topics/error-handling.md`: "Standout formats the message as `Error:
{error}` — the error's own `Display` text after that fixed prefix". Running it
confirmed: `brewlike plain` printed `Error: brewlike: no formula found:
obsidian`. The spec wants `brewlike: no formula found: obsidian` and nothing
else, so the prefix had to be routed around (see workarounds).

(5) `docs/guides/intro-to-testing.md`: "The `serial_test::serial` attribute is
re-exported from `standout_test` for convenience: `use standout_test::serial;`".
Doing exactly that fails to compile: `error[E0433]: cannot find module or crate
`serial_test` in this scope […] = note: this error originates in the attribute
macro `serial``. The expansion names the `serial_test` crate, so it has to be a
dev-dependency too.

(6) Cosmetic, and not adjustable from the application: `--output json` is
pretty-printed and its object keys go through a `serde_json::Map`, so
`brewlike list --output json` came out with `installed` before `name`, in a
multi-line document, while the spec illustrates compact documents with `name`
first. `docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md` documents the pretty-printing
(`serde_json::to_string_pretty(data)`); the key order I only found by running
it. I fixed the key order with a dependency feature (see workarounds) and left
the pretty-printing alone.

answers.summary:
`brewlike`, complete against SPEC.md except the section the spec itself marks
as the gap group. `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt
--check` and `cargo test` are all clean, and I verified every example in the
spec by running the compiled binary.

Layout (`app/src/`): `cellar.rs` is the CLI-free core — the frozen cellar plus
`find`, `closure`, `direct_dependencies` and `outdated`, with unit tests.
`view.rs` holds the serializable documents that *are* the machine contract:
`FormulaRecord`, `FormulaDetail`, `DependencyNode`, and a `#[serde(untagged)]`
`DependencyView` so `deps` can answer with an array of names or one tree node
under the same handler. `cli.rs` is the shell adapter: the clap surface, the
`#[derive(Dispatch)]` enum, four `#[handler]` functions, and `app()`. Four
templates in `src/templates/` and one stylesheet in `src/styles/`.

Verified behaviour: `list`, `info`, `deps`, `deps --tree` and `outdated`
render byte-for-byte as the spec shows (column padding computed from the
widest rendered cell, header included, one space between columns); `deps` on a
leaf prints zero bytes and exits 0; an empty `outdated` is the sentence, not a
headerless table; `--output json` produces the contracted root for each command
(array / record / array of names / nested node) and `[]` for an empty result;
unknown formula is exit 1 with `brewlike: no formula found: obsidian` on stderr
and nothing on stdout; no subcommand, unknown subcommand and unknown flag are
exit 2 with guidance on stderr and nothing on stdout; `--help` exits 0 on
stdout at every level.

Not implemented, deliberately: the "stamped form" (`schema_version` beside
`data`, and help-as-data in `--output json`). The spec names it as the
archetype's gap group (`PAR02`) and says the acceptance suite pins the
*unstamped* documents as what an implementation must produce now, so stamping
would have broken the criteria that are actually gradeable.

Tests: 9 unit tests (core + handler adapters, called directly as typed
functions) and 18 acceptance tests in `tests/acceptance.rs` driving the real
compiled binary through `standout_test::TestHarness::run_process`, since exit
codes, stream routing and exact bytes are settled at the process boundary.
answers.workarounds:
(1) `cli::app()` registers `.context_fn("view", |ctx| minijinja::Value::
from_serialize(ctx.data))`, a template-only mirror of the handler's own data
under one name. This exists solely because the array/record roots the machine
contract requires leave the templates with nothing to bind (friction 1). It is
a documented API used for an undocumented reason; a comment in `cli.rs` says
so. Structured output is untouched by it.

(2) `cli::domain_error` raises the unknown-formula diagnostic through
`ExternalFailure::new(1, format!("brewlike: {error}\n"))`.
`docs/topics/error-handling.md` scopes that type narrowly — "Use
`ExternalFailure` only when another operation owns the status and diagnostic
contract, such as a delegated Git invocation" — and here nothing external is
being delegated to. I used it because it is the only seam that emits an
application-owned diagnostic verbatim, without the `Error: ` prefix, and I own
the trailing newline (verified: stderr is exactly the 37 bytes ending `0a`).
The doc comment on the function records the reason.

(3) `serde_json = { version = "1", features = ["preserve_order"] }` in
`[dependencies]` is a feature-unification lever, not a code dependency: no
`brewlike` source file names `serde_json` outside the test suite. Turning the
feature on makes the framework's own `serde_json::Value` preserve insertion
order, which is what puts `name`, `installed`, `latest`, `outdated` in that
order in `--output json`. It is a global effect on a dependency I do not call,
so it is commented in `Cargo.toml`. JSON object key order is not semantically
meaningful, so removing this line loses nothing but the resemblance to the
spec's illustration.

(4) `serial_test = "3"` in `[dev-dependencies]`, needed only to satisfy the
expansion of `standout_test::serial` (docs gap 2).

None of these are in the domain code: `cellar.rs` and `view.rs` are free of all
four.
